newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa, UAP in Paris bourse spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Axa, UAP in Paris bourse spotlight.

text.p: Shares in French insurers Axa and Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) grabbed the spotlight on Thursday as they requoted for the first time since the two companies announced on Tuesday they planned to merge.
UAP shares exploded at the open, rising 17.19 percent from their close on November 8. The stock was the biggest gainer in the market on huge volume of nearly ten million shares by 1120 GMT.
It was by far the most heavily traded stock for the day.
At 1120 GMT, UAP shares were up 16 percent at 135.6 francs ($26.64).
"It's been totally, absolutely wild," said one trader. The trader said much of the action in the shares appeared to be from major international dealers acting on their own account.

Axa meanwhile was 4.87 percent lower at 303 francs in lesser but still heavy volume at 1045 GMT as investors reacted to the expected slight dilution of Axa share value from the merger which is set to occur through a stock swap.
In a surprising development, UAP shares were actually suspended limit-down after their surge at the open.
The stock exchange said this was because they had recalculated the value of UAP shares to take account of the terms of the planned stock swap, expected to be approved early next week.
The swap, which offers UAP shareholders four Axa shares and four certificates of guaranteed value for each ten UAP shares they hold, values UAP shares at 157 francs.

Though the certificates will not begin trading until the conclusion of the stock swap, French stock market authorities used the anticipated value of UAP shares after the swap to calculate upper and lower trading limits for Thursday's session.

Trading in shares is suspended in Paris when a stock moves ten percent in either direction from its last closing price. Without the recalculation, UAP shares would have been suspended limit up at the open.

As it was the revaluation of the shares, which put their lower limit at 135 francs, resulted in the surprising sight of UAP shares being briefly suspended limit down, despite trading nearly 16 percent higher than their November 8 close at the time.
Trading in UAP and Axa was calming but remained heavy, and traders said trading in the shares could well heat up later.
"It's calming down a bit but we'll have to see what the Americans do," said a trader. "They might want to get into this game.
-- Christopher Noble, Paris Newsroom +331 4221 5452 ($ = 5.089 French Francs)
